newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares shed gains, end lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares shed gains, end lower in thin trade.

text.p: Philippine shares on Wednesday failed to sustain early gains stumbling at close as concerns on the peso and interest rates outweighed cheer from higher first half earnings of two blue chip issues, traders said.
But turnover was light at 1.51 billion pesos.

"People are waiting for most companies to release their first half net profit figures, for the peso to become stable and for the interest rates to go down before plunging into equities," said Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities.
The main index closed 20.36 points lower, or 0.77 percent, at 2,636.37 points. Losers trounced gainers 100 to 26.
Petron Corp and the Philippine National Bank were among the first big firms to release first half net income.
The earnings of both firms were higher than last year.
The market however failed to sustain it's early gains.
The main index reached an intra-day high of 2,666.35 but fell into negative territory in midsession.

"It's probably the currency issue again as the Thai baht reached another record low early today. There's a psychological connection with the peso so with the baht's fall, some people feel the peso cannot be far behind," said Joey Roxas, president at Eagle Equities Inc.
Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co shares aided the fall as it was sold on news that it will incur losses if an international call rate cut takes place.
PLDT closed 30 pesos lower at 920 pesos.

"This consolidation may continue in the coming days. Investors feel they are trading blindly. They want the dust to settle in the foreign exchange market before they start sweeping the floor for bargains," said Jonathan Ravelas, sales head at Asian Capital Equities Inc.
But other traders said said stronger first half corporate earnings may dispel the lingering foreign exchange concerns.
